title: MBARI Summer Internship Program
description: A 10-week paid research or outreach internship at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) in Moss Landing, California, working on an ocean science, engineering, or marine research project under an MBARI mentor. Open to current undergraduate and graduate students, recent graduates planning to continue to graduate school, and educators at all levels, of any nationality. Interns are paid an hourly wage of USD 23/hour (full-time, roughly USD 3,984/month equivalent over the 10-week program), and MBARI arranges shared housing placement. Food, personal travel, and (for international applicants) visa costs and international airfare are not covered -- international applicants are welcome but must independently secure a US work visa if selected. Applicants must be at least 18 years old when the program starts. The application period for the next cycle closes at 8:00am Pacific time on February 9, 2027.
visaNote: International interns are responsible for securing their own US work visa (e.g., J-1 exchange visitor); MBARI does not sponsor or cover visa costs or international airfare.

title: Smithsonian Postgraduate/Postdoctoral Fellowship in Conservation of Museum Collections
description: A research fellowship at Smithsonian Institution museums and research units in the Washington, DC area, for recent graduates of master's programs in art/archaeological conservation (or equivalent) and materials scientists, including postdoctoral-level researchers, to conduct advanced research and training in the conservation of museum collection objects. Fellows are placed with a Smithsonian conservation staff member as advisor at a specific museum or unit (e.g. National Museum of Asian Art, National Museum of the American Indian). Duration is typically up to 12 months, with a minimum of 3 months. The postgraduate/predoctoral stipend is USD 45,000/year and the postdoctoral stipend is USD 57,000/year, both with a research allowance of up to USD 5,000/year for research-related travel and materials; some specific unit placements have additionally reported covering relocation travel, health insurance assistance, and visa/residence permit costs, though this is not guaranteed across all placements and should be confirmed with the specific hosting unit. Open to applicants of any nationality. Applications for the current annual cycle are due October 15, 2026.
visaNote: This is a research fellowship, not employment; non-US fellows should confirm visa arrangements with the specific hosting Smithsonian unit, as coverage of visa/residence permit costs varies by placement.
